claim: Albert Einstein arrived in Princeton in October 1933.

evidence.quote: 112 Mercer Street in Princeton, New Jersey, served as the residence of the renowned physicist Albert Einstein
Einstein purchased the home in 1935, having initially arrived in Princeton in October 1933 while fleeing Nazi persecution and assassination attempts.

notes: IAS article. The NHL nomination (EIN-S-0091) and NPS (EIN-S-0057) give the year only ('first came to Princeton in 1933').

notes: First Princeton residence (1933 stop). NHL nomination form (primary, NPS) and the NPS article (same holder, follows the nomination's wording).

claim: Albert Einstein purchased 112 Mercer Street in 1935.

evidence.quote: 112 Mercer Street in Princeton, New Jersey, served as the residence of the renowned physicist Albert Einstein from 1935 until his death in 1955.
Einstein purchased the home in 1935

notes: CONFLICT for owner decision: IAS (this source, owner of the house since 1986) says purchased 1935 and residence from 1935; the NHL nomination form (EIN-S-0091, primary) and NPS article (EIN-S-0057) say 'In 1936 he purchased 112 Mercer Street' (EIN-F-0106, verified). Not resolved by this run. The same IAS page also says the house was built in 1838 on Alexander Street and moved in the 1870s, while the NHL form says builder and date unknown, probably 1870s or 1880s (not staged).

claim: Albert Einstein covered the walls of his study with pictures of Michael Faraday, James Clerk Maxwell, and Isaac Newton.

evidence.quote: served as the residence of the renowned physicist Albert Einstein
Amidst the hustle and bustle of Princeton, 112 Mercer Street was a sanctuary for Einstein.

he covered the walls of his study with pictures of Michael Faraday, a pivotal figure in the fields of electromagnetism and electrochemistry; James Clerk Maxwell, who was responsible for the classical theory of electromagnetic radiation; and Isaac Newton

notes: Room-recreation detail for the Mercer Street study. Reconstructions may show these pictures only where a period photograph shows them.
